purpose: Close reading, writing guidance, complete table/method inventory and expanded two-part study design.

reading_record.technical_review: Main arguments, hypotheses, methods, variable definitions, all main and appendix tables and figures reviewed; bibliographies retained in extraction for traceability.
reading_record.locator_rule: PDF pages are one-based physical pages; printed page labels differ. Interpret all claims against the identified local version.

krueger_2023_local.title: The Effects of Mandatory ESG Disclosure Around the World

version.working_paper_cover: February 2023; ECGI Finance Working Paper 754/2021; SFI 21-44
version.rule: All detailed table and method statements below describe the supplied 2023 file, not an assumed identical 2024 article.

krueger_2023_local.research_question: Do mandatory ESG disclosures improve firm-level stock liquidity, and how do implementation, enforcement and prior information provision condition those effects?
contribution_architecture: Build a country-level regulatory dataset with policy details, rather than treating dates as externally given.
Estimate average market consequences in a global firm panel with several complementary liquidity outcomes.
Use regulatory implementation and institutional variation to interpret heterogeneity.
Examine firm information environments and then confront adoption endogeneity and staggered-estimation threats.

sample.note: Outcome-specific samples differ: Table 3 spreads N=136286, price impact N=137673, zero return N=137678; use column-specific denominators.

sources: government and exchange materials and media cross-checks
treatment.definition: Country indicator turns on when mandatory disclosure covers E, S and G. In gradual countries, use the last of the three topic dates.
scope_judgments: India coded 2015 when requirements extend to top 500 listed firms, rather than the 2012 top-100 phase.
Comply-or-explain belongs in the baseline mandatory category because an explanation is required.
Estonia and Slovakia have mandate dates but are absent from estimation because of missing market/control data.
France predates the panel, and Australia lacks a usable pre-period after lagging controls.
treatment.implication: An expanded policy inventory needs family-specific scope and date rules; a policy name or legal enactment is not sufficient to assign firm treatment.

hypotheses.claim: Liquidity improves after mandatory ESG disclosure.
hypotheses.competing_argument: Information may be unstructured, immaterial or cosmetic; prior voluntary disclosures may leave little incremental information.

hypotheses.claim: Government-issued rules produce larger liquidity improvements than exchange-issued rules.
Full compliance produces larger improvements than comply-or-explain.
Stronger formal institutions amplify liquidity benefits.
Stronger informal institutions amplify liquidity benefits.
Benefits are larger for firms not voluntarily providing earnings guidance.

outcomes.timing: Daily observations in the twelve months following fiscal year-end; indexed as t+1 relative to the regulatory year t.

bid_ask_spread.annual: Median daily spread; annual values below 0 or above 1 become missing; winsorize at 1st/99th percentiles; regress log spread.

price_impact.daily: Absolute total return in percent divided by USD trading value in thousands.
price_impact.annual: Median daily ratio multiplied by 1000; require at least 120 observations and price variation in the twelve-month window; winsorize at 1st/99th percentiles; regress log impact.
price_impact.unit_warning: A literal reading of the appendix percent-return/thousand-USD/multiply-by1000 wording implies1e8 times the decimal-return/USD-value ratio. Actual replication-code unit conventions were not verified. Preserve the unscaled ratio, state the chosen scaling, and do not claim numerical level replication; fixed rescaling cancels from log changes.

outcomes.zero_return: Zero-total-return trading days divided by potential trading days; this is neither dollar turnover nor observed return volatility.
outcomes.illiquidity_factor: Score of one factor extracted from log spread, log price impact and zero-return fraction; paper describes an oblique rotation. Larger values mean worse liquidity.

static: Active and dead constituent lists; common equity; major listing and primary ISIN; domestic firm on domestic exchange; adjusted-price availability.
Keep major domestic exchanges and drop exchanges with fewer than 30 firms.
Name, security-type and industry screens remove suspicious/noncommon-equity/investment-vehicle records following Ince-Porter, Campbell et al. and Griffin et al.
dynamic: Drop missing/negative closing prices and USD prices below 0.10.
For adjacent returns, if either exceeds 100% and their compounded two-day return is below 20%, set both returns missing.
Trading volume becomes missing when daily USD value traded is below 100.
screening.replication_caution: Current Parquets have primary-quote and security flags but not an audited historical constituent list, exact firm fiscal year-ends or the full original exchange/name/industry exclusions. Calendar-year estimates must be labeled an adaptation.

models.formula: L_i,c,t+1 = beta D_c,t + X_i,c,t-1 theta + firm_FE + industry_by_year_FE + error
models.clustering: Firm baseline; additional cluster structures tested in OA B2.
models.identification: Within-firm changes with industry-year shocks removed. Industry-year FE absorb general year effects; no country-year FE in this country-treatment baseline.

models.formula: L = beta1 D_X + beta2 D_notX + lagged controls + firm_FE + industry_by_year_FE + error
models.purpose: Separate nonoverlapping regulatory implementations and test beta1=beta2; do not infer a difference from separate significance stars.

models.formula: L = beta1 D*institution + beta2 D + beta3 institution + controls + fixed effects + error
models.purpose: Formal and informal enforcement moderation. Institutions are residualized on legal origin, GDP per capita and KOF globalization; residualizing is not a causal instrument.

models.formula: L = beta1 D*NoGuidance + beta2 D + beta3 NoGuidance + controls + fixed effects + error
models.purpose: Firm information environment; further interact partitions for issuing authority and compliance.

models.formula: AdoptionYear_c,t = beta1 GoogleSearch_c,t-1 + beta2 ESGIncidents_c,t-1 + error
models.purpose: Country-level diagnostic for observable adoption triggers; Google CSR, corporate social responsibility and ESG in separate specifications; RepRisk incidents included.
models.caution: A null association with selected proxies does not establish regulatory exogeneity.

tables.purpose: Make treatment coding and country composition visible.
tables.design_and_columns: Panel A: 35 treatment countries, dates, all-at-once, issuer, compliance, firm-years/shares, formal/informal norms and guidance. Panel B: 30 control countries and analogous coverage measures.
tables.reported_results: US contributes 54.1% of control firm-years; country shares are calculated within treatment/control panels.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Create family-by-country treatment register, eligible firm counts and evidence quality; distinguish known nonadoption from missing evidence.

tables.purpose: Show outcome scale, skewness, variation and overlap.
tables.design_and_columns: Panel A mean, SD, P5, median, P95 and N; Panel B liquidity correlations, all on the factor baseline sample.
tables.reported_results: Mean spread .008, median .003; zero fraction .080; factor SD .902. Log spread/log impact correlation .79.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Use a common complete-case outcome sample for comparability plus outcome-specific coverage; document factor construction and units.

tables.purpose: Estimate average effects and challenge key sample choices.
tables.design_and_columns: 11 columns: three individual outcomes; factor baseline; firm/year FE; before 2010; 2010 onward; treated countries only; pre/post collapse; all-at-once vs gradual; exclude gradual.
tables.reported_results: Baseline log spread -.084 (SE .011), log impact -.161 (.019), zero -.015 (.001), factor -.085 (.007). Factor baseline N=136269, 17680 firms, 65 countries, 44% never-treated; adjusted R2 .897.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Put family-specific effects and clean cohort comparisons first; report countries and independent policy clusters, not just security-years.
tables.limitations: OLS staggered comparisons can use already-treated controls; treated-only sample is not itself a solution. exp(beta)-1 gives exact log percentage change; -.084 is about -8.1%, not exactly -8.4%.

tables.design_and_columns: Six columns: government only, exchange only, both; binding only, comply-or-explain only, both. Same controls and FE. F-tests compare the paired coefficients.
tables.reported_results: Joint government -.102 vs exchange -.037, reported p=.000; binding -.098 vs comply-or-explain -.068, p=.030.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Code issuer and compliance explicitly per policy; distinguish legally required public information from confidential submissions.
tables.limitations: Issuer/compliance differences are not randomly assigned; p=.000 is rounded, never literal zero.

tables.purpose: Evaluate formal versus informal enforcement moderation.
tables.design_and_columns: Five columns: residualized rule of law and government effectiveness (Panel A), EPI environment, IVS environment and IVS social norms (Panel B); main effects included.
tables.reported_results: Formal interactions .004 and -.022 are not significant; EPI -.003, IVS E -.467 and IVS S -.564 are significant. N=121353 or 120555; 60 or 55 countries.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Use conceptually relevant institutions for each family, measured before treatment; do not apply ESG norms mechanically to confidential tax or crypto rules.

tables.purpose: Test whether initial information provision moderates effects.
tables.design_and_columns: Three columns: D*NoGuidance; issuer-specific interactions; compliance-specific interactions, with constituent main effects.
tables.reported_results: D*NoGuidance -.037 (.016); government interaction -.070; exchange -.007; binding -.040; comply/explain -.024.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Use actual guidance/coverage data if available. A stock-liquidity proxy is not equivalent to managerial guidance.
tables.limitations: Body says +.037 then calls it negative; table/economic argument show -.037. Also distinguish an incremental interaction from the total treatment effect for a subgroup.

tables.purpose: Probe observable political or incident triggers of adoption.
tables.design_and_columns: Six country regressions: three search terms for 35 mandate countries (N452) and for 20 all-at-once countries (N257); common RepRisk regressor; data effectively 2007-2020.
tables.reported_results: No search or incident regressor is significant; adjusted R2 is slightly negative.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Use family-specific policy-attention and incident measures; report weak power and the restricted adopter-only sample.
tables.limitations: This is an event-year regression, not the JIBS status model or a fully specified first-adoption hazard.

tables.purpose: Check staggered treatment heterogeneity with clean controls.
tables.design_and_columns: Four columns: Callaway-SantAnna without/with controls; stacked without/with controls. Never/not-yet-treated controls; firm/year or firm-stack/year-stack effects.
tables.reported_results: ATT estimates -.050, -.105, -.137, -.129 respectively; all significant in the supplied file.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Make cohort-time effects the main specification; freeze aggregation weights, report support and avoid already-treated controls.
tables.limitations: The table omits sample counts and cohort details; a new paper should report these. Stacking requires explicit duplication weights; do not label any hand-built comparison a complete Callaway-SantAnna replication.

tables.design_and_columns: SS1-SS8 firm/security/exchange/name screens; duplicated SS6 label in the PDF.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Provide a field-by-field availability and implemented-screen mapping.

tables.design_and_columns: DS1-DS4 price, return spike/reversal, quote and turnover filters.
tables.reported_results: Thresholds: .10 USD, 200%, 100%/20% reversal, 100 USD trading value.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Log attrition per filter and validate return units before applying.

tables.design_and_columns: Country and exchange mnemonic list, including some countries absent from final sample.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Audit trading venue against issuer domicile and rule jurisdiction; do not infer firm domicile solely from trading currency.

tables.design_and_columns: Country, date, venue, regulation and issuer for 35 mandates.
tables.reported_results: Contains the paper coding rather than a fresh legal audit.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Maintain source URLs, locators, date kind, scope and national versus supranational choice for every family.

tables.purpose: Test model, cluster, concentration and anticipation sensitivity.
tables.design_and_columns: Seven columns: industry-country FE; add country linear/quadratic trends; exclude US/Japan/UK/Korea; country-year clusters; country clusters; industry-year clusters; omit year -1.
tables.reported_results: Effects remain negative; baseline -.085 has SE .019 country-year, .028 country and .011 industry-year; omitting -1 gives -.095.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Country-level or policy-cluster inference should be primary for country treatments; preserve all pre-specified sensitivities.
tables.limitations: Body refers to year clustering in one place, but OA B2 labels country; follow the table and record the discrepancy.

figures.content: Separate E/S/G timelines; gray means simultaneous adoption, brackets mean incomplete ESG coverage, asterisks mark the last topic.
figures.transfer: Use family-specific timelines with date-type and coordination legends.

figures.content: Event time relative to -1; tails binned <=-3 and >=+3; 99% intervals; firm/year FE specification based on Table 3 column 5.
figures.reading: A positive lead at -2 is visible. The discussion interprets the decline into -1 as possible anticipation; the claim of little pretrend is not proof of parallel trends.
figures.transfer: Report exact liquidity-year versus policy-year alignment, joint lead test, simultaneous intervals and anticipation sensitivity; avoid treating a lead-test failure to reject as verification.

robustness_inventory: Alternative fixed effects; early/late calendar subperiods; treated-only sample; pre/post collapse; simultaneous versus gradual mandates; exclude gradual countries.
Drop largest countries; country-specific linear and quadratic trends; alternative cluster levels; omit immediately preceding year.
Event study with lead and lag bins; observed policy-attention/incident trigger regressions.
Callaway-SantAnna and stacked estimates with and without controls.
identification_appraisal: Parallel trends remains a maintained counterfactual assumption; many treated countries do not logically guarantee it.
Within-firm FE do not eliminate unobserved country-time reforms or spillovers. Treatment-country comparisons do not remove cross-border information spillovers.
Firm clustering may understate dependence for country decisions; OA country clustering is particularly relevant.
No-dynamic-treatment-effects is a requirement for some TWFE comparisons, not for every modern cohort-specific DiD estimator.
Institutional residuals, issuer partitions and lack of significance in adoption-trigger models do not establish exogeneity.
The empirical evidence is strongest when outcome, scope, timing and comparison-group assumptions are explicit rather than inferred from significance.

text_table_discrepancies.locator: printed p24 / PDF29 and Table3 / PDF52
text_table_discrepancies.detail: All-at-once versus one-by-one equality test: prose .6067, table .6967. Do not silently reconcile.

text_table_discrepancies.locator: printed p30 / PDF35 and Table6 / PDF56
text_table_discrepancies.detail: Prose initially says interaction .037 but immediately describes a negative estimate; table -.037.

text_table_discrepancies.locator: printed p25 footnote29 / PDF30 and OA B2 / PDF70
text_table_discrepancies.detail: Body mentions year clustering; table column5 is country clustering.
Leverage row includes a misplaced market-price/book-equity phrase. Resolve definitions from source items and the intended debt/assets definition.
Reported all-at-once mean .186 plus one-by-one mean .127 exceeds baseline .306 despite the described exhaustive partition. Check replication data before using partition shares.

writing_analysis.voice: Restrained empirical first-person plural. The authors introduce the economic question early, state what they measure, and connect each table to a specific inference.
introduction_moves: Begin with an investor information problem and the regulatory response.
State the dataset and outcome; justify liquidity through economic relevance, comparability and links to prior financial-disclosure work.
Give sample scale and treatment variation before interpreting results.
Present opposing theoretical channels so the sign remains an empirical question.
Preview main magnitudes and robustness, then implementation, enforcement and firm heterogeneity.
Acknowledge a concrete confounder and summarize the relevant diagnostic.
Place the contribution among cross-country and single-country literatures with specific differences.
results_paragraph_moves: Economic magnitude in units or SD
Formal difference test when comparing groups
writing_analysis.table_design: Numbered columns, dependent-variable spanners, estimate/SE pairs, concise FE and control rows, sample qualifications, N/firms/countries, never-treated share and R2; detailed standalone notes define variables, time indices, sources and clustering.
sentence_practice: Use concrete measurement verbs and explicit referents rather than vague claims of robustness.
Separate the sign of illiquidity from the economic direction of liquidity.
State a null finding without converting it into proof of no mechanism.
Translate log points with exp(beta)-1, and report denominators for SD or percent changes.
Use the table as evidence within connected paragraphs, not a chronological list of every coefficient.
original_sentence_examples_for_our_paper: We examine whether the market consequences of disclosure rules differ with the audience that receives the information.
The comparison holds the outcome definition constant while allowing regulatory scope and implementation dates to vary across policy families.
The estimate describes market-wide changes around documented implementation; firm eligibility has not yet been established.
The absence of a precise association leaves the learning prediction unresolved in this sample.
avoid: Copying the source prose or carrying its positive results into the new abstract.
Calling calendar-year market aggregates an exact firm-level fiscal-year replication.
Declaring all robustness checks passed because some coefficients retain stars.
Treating additional policy families as independent observations when they share legal acts and adoption dates.

koning_2018_jibs.title: Drivers of institutional change around the world The case of IFRS
koning_2018_jibs.question: Which intercountry mechanisms explain the extent and pattern of national IFRS adoption?

conceptual_framework.qualification: The authors acknowledge that centrally coordinated coercion does not meet a strict decentralized-diffusion definition, but include it to test international organizational pressure.

sample.reason_for_EU_exclusion: Coordinated IFRS adoption is not an independent national diffusion decision.
sample.model_specific_samples: Primary combined binary and ordinal models N1456 /142 countries; domestic-control combined model N1383 /138 countries.

dependent_variables.binary: Country-year status equals 1 when IFRS is required for some or all domestic firms; 0 otherwise within the coded sample.
dependent_variables.scope: Domestic listed/unlisted companies excluding financial institutions; listed/publicly accountable entities can count as full mandatory adoption under the authors interpretation.
dependent_variables.timing_and_content: Code actual IFRS reference and an updating/adoption policy. Mere convergence to modified standards or an old frozen IAS/IFRS version is not necessarily adoption.
dependent_variables.important_distinction: These are repeated adoption-status logits and ordinal logits, not clearly an at-risk first-adoption hazard with postadoption rows dropped. Do not relabel them as such.

sources_and_validation: Historical IAS Plus and IFRS in Your Pocket
ROSC and national legal materials to resolve contradictions

mechanisms.name: competition
mechanisms.primary: For each country-year form its export-share vector across partners; correlate country-pair export patterns; select five highest-correlation competitors; compute the share that adopted IFRS.
mechanisms.alternative: Share of IFRS adopters in the same EIU country-risk class; risk averages sovereign, currency and banking-sector ratings.
mechanisms.not_equivalent: An outward portfolio-holdings weighted adoption share measures financial exposure; it is not the paper export-similarity or same-risk competition measure.

mechanisms.name: learning
mechanisms.primary: Among ten nearest geographic neighbors, indicator that median GDP growth of IFRS adopters exceeds median growth of nonadopters.
mechanisms.edge_cases: No adopter gives 0. If all ten adopted, compare adopter median growth to growth of the focal country.
mechanisms.alternative: Replace GDP growth with GDP-per-capita growth.
mechanisms.identification_limit: Observed GDP success is not an estimate of the causal effect of IFRS; the construct is perceived success, not demonstrated policy benefit.

mechanisms.name: coercion
mechanisms.primary: IMF/World Bank credit or foreign aid relative to GDP. Narrative wording varies between credit/aid; Table1 defines amounts and source.
mechanisms.alternative: Indicator of receipt of IMF or World Bank resources.
mechanisms.qualification: Organizational dependence, not a network adoption share; receiving money alone is not proof of an IFRS condition.

mechanisms.name: emulation
mechanisms.primary: Share of IFRS adopters among ten closest countries in Berry et al administrative/cultural distance, combining legal systems, colonial ties, language and religion.
mechanisms.alternative: IFAC professional-body membership status: 0 no registered body; 1 affiliate; 2 associate; 3 full member.
mechanisms.qualification: Professional advocacy may be endogenous. One-year lags improve chronology but do not by themselves solve reverse causality.

estimation.lag: All diffusion and domestic covariates lag one year.
estimation.fixed_effects: Year indicators; no country fixed effects are shown in the main tables.
estimation.errors: Country-clustered robust SE; note4 reports robustness to two-way country/time clustering and alternative LR specifications including Bartolucci-Nigro.
estimation.reporting: Exponentiated coefficients and corresponding SE are odds ratios; an odds ratio does not equal a probability effect.
domestic_controls: EU exports / total exports (Table1 wording; body once says GDP)
estimation.caution: Table1 assigns zero to missing market capitalization. The new study should retain missing values and report coverage rather than reproduce that convention.

tables.design_and_columns: Binary/ordinal outcomes; two measures per mechanism; six domestic controls; definitions, N, mean, SD, min/max and sources.
tables.reported_results: Dependent-variable observations 1746; competition capital-risk measure 1024, demonstrating unequal coverage.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Construct a comparable data dictionary with missingness and temporal availability; preserve source-quality distinctions.

tables.purpose: Test mechanisms separately and jointly using binary adoption status.
tables.design_and_columns: Five logits: one per primary mechanism and all four together; year FE, lagged covariates, country SE; odds ratios.
tables.reported_results: Joint ORs: competition 1.669; learning 1.707; coercion .622; emulation 7.872. Learning/emulation strongest; N1456/142 clusters.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Include separate and joint mechanism models on a common sample as well as maximal samples; avoid attributing changes solely to additional controls when N changes.

tables.purpose: Use adoption intensity instead of a binary collapse.
tables.design_and_columns: Same five specifications as Table2 but ordinal status 0-4.
tables.reported_results: Joint ORs: competition 2.044; learning 1.834; coercion .296; emulation 7.759; N1456/142 clusters.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Only estimate ordinal models if comparable ordered adoption stages are actually coded; the current 14-family ledger has no universal ordinal scale.
tables.limitations: The supplied paper does not report a formal proportional-odds test; include one before relying on an analogous ordered model.

tables.design_and_columns: Eight ordinal models: substitute each alternative mechanism alone and jointly with the other three primary measures.
tables.reported_results: Alternative capital competition OR8.425 alone and12.157 joint, with only1024/986 observations; alternative learning OR1.414/1.397; IFAC1.312/1.237; coercion not supported.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Predefine alternate networks, success definitions and common-sample comparisons; scale ORs by interpretable changes, such as a 10pp adoption share.

tables.purpose: Compare diffusion with domestic demand explanations.
tables.design_and_columns: Domestic controls alone; each mechanism plus domestic controls; all four plus controls. Six ordinal models, year FE and country SE.
tables.reported_results: Joint ORs competition2.540, learning1.749, coercion1.253, emulation5.389; regulatory quality1.945; N1383/138 countries.
tables.application_to_expanded_paper: Keep domestic controls conceptually motivated and lagged. Country clustering does not absorb time-invariant country heterogeneity.
tables.limitations: Body suggests clustering handles time-invariant country influences; clustering adjusts uncertainty and is not a country fixed effect.

figure.purpose: Two-axis conceptual map before operationalization, separating motives from empirical proxies.

appendix.purpose: Explain triangulation, IFRS adoption categories, treatment of convergence/old standards and contradiction resolution.

writing_analysis.framing: Begin from the surprising worldwide institutional change and its relevance for MNE strategy, then explain the gap left by static institutional theories.
writing_analysis.theory: Define a small number of distinct mechanisms before describing their proxies. Acknowledge overlap and imperfect measurement.
writing_analysis.empirical_sequence: Sampling and unit choice; dependent coding; primary/alternative measures for each mechanism; domestic factors; binary then ordinal tests; alternative measures; controls.
writing_analysis.discussion: Translate mechanism associations back to whose interests and ideas can change international institutions; distinguish business benefits from political/professional drivers.
writing_analysis.transfer: Use this conceptual precision to organize Part2, but retain Krueger-style measurement and table discipline. Avoid copying broad causal claims from observational status models.

nontransferable_assumptions: IFAC advocacy is specific to accounting standards and is not automatically a relevant emulation measure for crypto, supply chains or tax reporting.
A common EU legal date represents coordination, not independent national peer influence.
The ordered IFRS policy categories cannot be recreated merely from the presence of an event in an incomplete expanded ledger.
Estimated liquidity effects using later data cannot be inserted into earlier adoption decisions as if policymakers observed them.

expanded_study.working_title: Global disclosure policies stock liquidity and international diffusion

two_parts.question: How do liquidity changes around disclosure regulation differ across policy families, information audiences and implementation designs?
two_parts.target_estimand: Family-specific firm-eligible cohort-time ATT, followed by a transparent cross-family aggregation on common support.
two_parts.current_feasible_estimand: Descriptive calendar-year security/country liquidity changes around first recorded national implementations; optional clean not-yet-recorded-event comparisons conditional on documented adopters.
two_parts.distinction: A timing association in a partial event inventory is not an identified global policy ATT.

two_parts.question: Does prior adoption by connected countries, and the success they visibly experience, predict later independent national adoption?
two_parts.target_estimand: First-adoption hazard among verified at-risk country-family-years; secondary adoption-status or ordinal models only with adequate status histories.
two_parts.current_feasible_estimand: Conditional timing models among documented independent national implementations, with explicit limits from case selection and unverified prior histories.

family_scope_rules.IFRS: Public financial information; listed/consolidated scope and national implementation phases matter.
family_scope_rules.ESG_CSR: Public nonfinancial reporting; preserve E/S/G coverage, bindingness and size phases; 39 proxy dates are a separate sensitivity sample.
family_scope_rules.CLIMATE: Public climate information but phased issuer coverage; no substitution of announcement for first required reporting.
family_scope_rules.ISSB: Standards issuance, voluntary application and binding national adoption differ; recent cohorts may have no complete postwindow.
family_scope_rules.XBRL: Reporting format affects accessibility; exchange, filing type and firm-size phases matter.
family_scope_rules.GOVERNANCE: Public compliance/explanation and governance changes may operate together; cannot isolate information alone automatically.
family_scope_rules.BENEFICIAL_OWNERSHIP: Entity ownership records, public access and register restrictions differ; does not necessarily treat all listed firms.
family_scope_rules.CBCR_CONFIDENTIAL: Tax-authority information; a liquidity effect need not arise from direct investor access. Keep separate from public CbCR.
family_scope_rules.CBCR_PUBLIC: Sector-specific banking and general multinational reporting differ; fiscal start and first public filing are distinct.
family_scope_rules.AUDIT_REPORTING: Expanded auditor reporting/KAM disclosure; applicable engagements and listing segments matter.
family_scope_rules.AUDIT_OVERSIGHT: Mix of oversight-body establishment, registration and rotation; split subtypes before causal pooling.
family_scope_rules.EXTRACTIVE_PAYMENTS: Sector-specific public payments; all-market averages dilute eligibility.
family_scope_rules.SUPPLY_CHAIN: Sector/size/supply-chain obligations; reporting and due-diligence duties differ.
family_scope_rules.DIGITAL_ASSET: Crypto-market rules and MiCA components need not treat ordinary listed equities; other channels may drive any equity association.

timing_contract.primary_rule: Align eligibility and outcome measurement with the first required report becoming available; show fiscal-start timing as a sensitivity when disclosure dates are uncertain.
timing_contract.pilot_rule: Event year remains the ledger reporting/implementation year; outcome at policy year+1 is calendar-year, not fiscal-year aligned.
timing_contract.unknowns: No absent ledger record becomes a never-adopted control; retain missing policy histories and incomplete-census flags.

identification_and_inference: Start from country-family-specific eligible firms, separately assessing direct public disclosure and indirect/confidential channels.
Estimate cohort-time effects against verified not-yet/never-treated units; avoid using already-treated countries as untreated controls.
Hold the set of securities constant between baseline and follow-up within each cohort comparison to reduce composition changes.
Report calendar support, country/cohort counts and independent legal-cluster counts. Cluster at policy assignment level; assess few-cluster inference.
Model overlapping reforms and common legal acts; show isolated-event windows and exclusion of coordinated EU waves.
Predefine outcome/family multiplicity and report adjusted inference alongside all estimates, including nulls.
For learning use only returns, trading or liquidity changes actually observable before the focal adoption. Label realized changes as perceived success, never causal benefits by construction.
Cross-fit any estimated foreign policy benefit so the focal country and future data do not generate its own explanatory signal.
Include network adoption separately from success interactions so learning is not merely relabeled exposure.
Distinguish competition networks (export similarity or competing investment destinations), emulation networks (legal/cultural ties), and actual coercive policy conditions.

Current first draft uses only descriptive liquidity point comparisons and assignment-cluster deletion ranges; modern eligible-firm causal estimators and formal policy-effect inference remain a subsequent stage.

planned_table_sequence.content: Policy families, audiences, dates, scope, sources and evidence quality; documented implementations versus proxy/future/coordinated records.
Raw-market attrition and outcome distributions/correlations, countries and quote/security coverage.
Family-specific liquidity estimates with eligible-firm and cohort support, three individual outcomes and optional validated factor.
Clean estimator, timing, anticipation, overlap, sample and cluster sensitivities; adjustment across outcomes/families.
Public versus confidential channel, authority, compliance and baseline institutional heterogeneity; formal coefficient-difference tests.
Network definitions, descriptive adoption shares and success signals; case-universe/risk-set attrition.
Competition, learning, emulation and coercion separately and jointly; independent national choices primary.
Alternative networks, lag lengths, GDP versus liquidity success, common samples, hazard versus status and coordination sensitivities.

reporting_rules: Every empirical statement names its sample and estimand.
Distinguish estimated, descriptive, planned, unavailable and failed tests using explicit status fields.
Do not use old 59-country environmental pilot estimates as results of the new 14-family panel.
A family with insufficient support remains in the inventory and receives an explicit non-estimation reason.
A draft can present measured results while clearly identifying which causal claims remain unsupported.

external_method_sources.title: Difference-in-Differences with Multiple Time Periods
external_method_sources.use: Cohort-time comparisons and explicit aggregation; not-yet-treated comparison groups.

external_method_sources.title: Published Krueger et al article
external_method_sources.use: Bibliographic version check only; local January2023 file controls the close reading.

results_status: Expanded weighting, robustness and JIBS-inspired mechanism follow-up completed with observed inputs; no global causal effect or robust diffusion mechanism established.

summary.reason: Partial policy histories, unverified firm eligibility, heterogeneous date meanings and overlapping/coordinated reforms; estimates are descriptive conditional timing/comparison evidence.

unestimated_mechanisms.emulation: No audited family-relevant cultural/administrative peer and professional-advocacy histories constructed.
unestimated_mechanisms.coercion: No verified time-varying family-specific policy conditionality instrument constructed.

limitations: Fiscal dates cover the ESG subset, not the whole quote universe. Historical quote-to-company mapping is not audited.

return_consistency.purpose: Interpret return-index consistency checks without replacing vendor returns arbitrarily.
checks: A within-chunk April2007 probe found no displayed return/RI mismatch under the stated sample filter.
A boundary-window probe displayed20 large differences between vendor ret and adjacent observed RI returns; displayed records were Monday quotes in SA, IL and EG.
return_consistency.interpretation: The pattern is consistent with differences between the vendor last-local-trading-date return and the return between available extract dates. Missing local trading dates or stale quotes are possible explanations; they have not been exhaustively reconciled.
return_consistency.consequence: Retain the documented vendor return field. Do not overwrite it with RI ratios across gaps or label every audit difference an erroneous return. The current zero-return denominator remains observed valid dates, and exact exchange calendars are a required extension.
return_consistency.claim_limit: No exhaustive validation of every daily return or local trading calendar is asserted.

availability_cautions: Market observations predate the focal year, but portfolio publication/revision lags and historical security-selection lookahead remain unaudited.
No source-paper estimated effect is presented as an estimate from this expanded data.
Formal liquidity-effect inference is withheld; recorded-case comparisons use deletion sensitivity ranges.

dictionary.security_id: Datastream infocode quote identifier. A complete historical issuer consolidation has not been established.
dictionary.country2: Quote trading region after domestic-company/primary-quote filters.
dictionary.iso3: Current ISO crosswalk; historical state existence not reconciled.
dictionary.year: Calendar market year; not an issuer fiscal-year label.
dictionary.G: First recorded implementation year in the dated source register, not globally verified first legal adoption.
dictionary.event: 1 at G and0 earlier in the documented-case timing sample; not a full legal policy-status series.
dictionary.spread: Annual median relative bid-ask spread with120-day minimum, annual range[0,1], and year-specific1/99 winsorization.
dictionary.impact: Annual median absolute decimal local total return / USD trading value, times1e8 under literal reference-appendix unit interpretation. Unscaled amihud_per_usd is retained; do not claim level replication without vendor-unit reconciliation.
dictionary.zero_fraction: Zero-return days / observed valid-return days;120-day minimum and price variation. Not an independently audited potential-trading-day denominator.
dictionary.log_spread: Natural log of positive winsorized spread.
dictionary.log_impact: Natural log of positive winsorized impact. Fixed rescaling cancels from within-security log differences.
dictionary.liquidity_improvement: Negative one-year difference of country mean log spread, requiring consecutive years and at least30 valid quote observations per country-year.
dictionary.exposure: t-1 portfolio weight in countries whose first recorded implementation is no later than t-1. Unknown histories remain explicit in unclassified_weight.
dictionary.classified_weight: Portfolio share in partners with a dated family record, including records whose date is later. This is a retrospective case classification, not independent verification of all earlier legal states.
dictionary.unclassified_weight: One minus classified_weight; preserved rather than calling these holdings legally untreated.
dictionary.learning: t-1 portfolio-weighted foreign liquidity improvement among partners with recorded implementation by t-2. Requires80% signal coverage among those partners; defined0 for an empty earlier-implementer set only.
dictionary.ln_market_cap: Observed log summed annual median quote market cap, lagged exactly one calendar year in timing regressions.
dictionary.ln_dollar_volume: Observed log summed valid annual USD trading value, lagged one year.
dictionary.return_volatility: Country median of annual quote-level daily total-return SD, lagged one year in models.
dictionary.stratum: Family-year category used as an intercept in timing logits; constant-outcome strata excluded from fitting.
dictionary.estimate: Balanced-security equal-country cohort comparison aggregated by contributing treated-country counts; descriptive conditional on documented cases.
dictionary.loco_low_and_loco_high: Range after deleting one recorded assignment cluster at a time and reconstructing supported cohorts. A composition-sensitive robustness range, not a confidence interval.
dictionary.holm_p: Multiplicity adjustment for estimable timing coefficients. Liquidity-effect p-values are withheld in this draft.
dictionary.source_benchmark: Separate35-treated/30-control published2023 sample through2020; source dates remain publication coding and do not alter the verified implementation register.

liquidity.factor: PC1 of standardized original three proxies; fit only on complete2000-2004 quote observations, freeze means/scales/loadings, orient positive illiquidity; report loadings/variance and complete-case counts.
liquidity.additional_measure_definition: Log annual USD traded value divided by within-year median USD market capitalization, requiring120 impact days and positive denominator; not exact share turnover. Daily-return SD requires120 return days and price variation.
liquidity.weight_timing: GDP and market cap fixed at g-1 for treated and control countries. Normalize within cohort arms; aggregate cohorts by treated weight mass. Each weighted design has an equal-country comparison on exactly its eligible country/cohort support.
liquidity.primary_comparison: g+1 versus g-1; same quote-country units observed in both years; at least30 units per country and3 later-case control countries per cohort.
liquidity.robustness_matrix: Baseline: all6 outcomes x all6 country weights, plus same-sample equal baselines. Other configurations: original three proxies plus factor x equal-country and constant-GDP weights; no arbitrary Cartesian combinations of filters.
liquidity.balanced_dynamic_profile: Quotes and countries observed at every g-3..g+3; controls have recorded G>g+3; g-1 reference; compare equal and constant-GDP weights. Constant supporting sample within each family-outcome profile.
liquidity.sensitivity: Assignment-cluster deletion ranges, concentration, maximum treated weight, effective weighted treated-country count; ranges are not confidence intervals. Report every unsupported cell and attrition.
liquidity.formal_inference: No causal-effect p-values from the incomplete case inventory. Do not relabel deletion ranges as confidence intervals or descriptive event profiles as validated causal event studies.

diffusion.source_reference: Koning, Mertens and Roosenboom2018 JIBS, supplied PDF pages7-10,Tables2-5. Primary source trade measure is mean adoption among five most correlated export-pattern competitors; learning is relative median GDP growth among ten geographic neighbors; cultural/admin peers are distinct from expert-community IFAC advocacy.
diffusion.source_coverage: Conditional on documented cases. Exclude coordinated focal cases using existing national-choice flag. Main competitor share is among observed dated neighbors only, requiring3of5 known neighbors; report missing fraction and bounds. Strict sensitivity requires4of5. Neighbors are selected before inspecting policy adoption status.
diffusion.trade_data: COW raw directional flows, not smoothed series. Negative/missing flows remain missing; Pearson correlation on at least20 jointly observed destination markets. Deterministic ISO tie break. No future-year trade weights.
diffusion.learning: Foreign recorded G<=t-2; growth or liquidity observed no later than t-1; later-case comparators recorded G>t-1. Geographic nearest10 selected independently of policy data. Require at least one measured earlier and later case and80percent signal coverage in both groups. Missing comparison groups remain missing. Benchmarked success uses g-1..g+1 balanced-quote contrasts available by t-1, excludes focal-country and its assignment cluster from foreign controls; at least3 remaining controls.
diffusion.coercion: WDI credit series includes SDR allocations; aid is not policy conditionality. Preserve missing observations, including nonreporting higher-income countries. Report standalone components and combined author-style proxy; no claim of verified coercion.
diffusion.emulation: Language, legal-origin and general IGO peer exposure are partial proxies. No claim to reproduce Berry cultural/admin composite without religion or to replace IFAC professional advocacy. Historical source availability/snapshot limits retained.
diffusion.likelihood: Binomial logit; family-year stratum fixed effects, after excluding constant-outcome strata. Country-cluster covariance, Student-t reference with countries-1df. LPM uses same sample and fixed effects. Standardize continuous slopes within exact estimation sample; record all dropped constant nuisance terms and rank checks.
diffusion.stability: Converged, no estimation warnings, finite coefficients/SE, abs coefficient below25 and full-rank design; otherwise retain diagnostics and withhold interpretation.
diffusion.multiplicity: Holm across every estimable new focal coefficient, with raw and adjusted p-values. Also identify the narrower primary family. Single and combined fits and LPM sensitivity are disclosed, never chosen for significance.
diffusion.no_real_time_claim: Feature calendar dates precede focal year; historical releases, current vintage revisions and historical quote selection remain unaudited. Fixed2000 and fixed2013 networks are distinct specifications, not imputed annual observations.

writing_principles: Define the economic construct before presenting its proxy.
Explain each table's exact sample, timing and unit before interpreting coefficients.
Connect magnitude and economic meaning, with conditional-design limits stated in the same paragraph.
Distinguish descriptive comparisons, nominal inference and multiplicity-adjusted inference.
Report unsupported/null/unstable results without switching specifications for favorable signs.
